intro: Three free pieces I think are worth your time this week, chosen from the Substacks I follow most closely. Each one opens on the writer's own Substack.

items.title: Yes, Writing Does Advance Thinking
items.why: With end-of-year writing tasks everywhere, I loved Wexler's clear case for why writing about what students have learned deepens their thinking, in every subject and not just English.

items.title: Research Bite #77: Understanding the equals sign and solving equivalence problems
items.why: A quick, practical read for anyone teaching maths in the primary years. In this study nearly half of students finishing primary school read the equals sign as 'work out the answer', and those who saw it as meaning 'the same value' did better.

items.title: Is Understanding Just "Remembering in Disguise"?
items.why: If you've ever heard memorisation and understanding set up as opposites, read this. Hendrick unpacks a new paper by John Sweller and colleagues arguing that understanding comes from remembering ideas that interact, which matters for how we plan explanations.
